description.narrative: Det svenska stödet till Diakonia initierades av ambassaden för att ge stöd till civilsamhället i Uganda genom en svensk organisation med god kapacitet och kompetens inom främjande av demokrati och mänskliga rättigheter (MR). Diakonias fokus i Uganda är främjande av MR och demokrati, jämställdhet, social och ekonomisk rättvisa samt konflikthantering. Det planerade svenska stödet är 30 MSEK under 3 år

The Swedish support to Diakonia was an initiative of the Embassy to support CSOs in Uganda through a Swedish Organisation with strong competences and capacity in the area of Democracy and Human rights promotion. Diakonias focus in Uganda is Promotion of Human Rights and Democracy, Gender Equity, Social Economic Justice & Conflict management. The proposed 3 year Swedesh support is 30 MSEK.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2014Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: An evaluation was commissioned at the end of the two phases of the programme (2008-2011 and 2011-2014) The evaluation found that the programme had been relevant both to the local and national contexts and to the Swedish cooperation strategy with Uganda. Diakonia has been supporting strategic actors within the civil society and the partners show interesting results particularly at local level for specific rights-holders and duty-bearers. The progressively stronger focus on HRBA and gender equality had further enhanced the relevance of the programme.
The programme has been able to deliver several important changes at local level. Some of the most interesting outcomes are related to the empowerment of women and girls and changed attitudes towards gender equality at community level and among local duty-bearers. Change has started taking shape at individual level, but a critical mass of individuals has yet to be reached, and it is therefore not possible to claim that the programme has so far promoted major societal changes.
On an overall level the programme management is found to be sound and the size of the country office reasonable. Diakonia has been able to focus more on results-based management during the latter part of the programme and it was evident that partners now try to focus on processes of change rather than on activity outputs. This area needs to be strengthened and partners, as well as Diakonia’s country team, need to develop their skills on how to document and measure the changes they claim to see.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
